article_title: NTA: India's high-stakes exam system faces a crisis of trust

tasks.prompt: What is the central argument of the article?
options: India's exam crisis involves not only paper leaks but also weaknesses in the NTA's structure and an over-reliance on centralised, one-off high-stakes tests
India should replace all university admissions with private interviews immediately
The NTA has never conducted a successful examination
Computer-based testing alone has already restored complete public trust
tasks.correct_answer: India's exam crisis involves not only paper leaks but also weaknesses in the NTA's structure and an over-reliance on centralised, one-off high-stakes tests
tasks.explanation_hebrew: הכתבה טוענת שהמשבר רחב מדליפות: הוא כולל מבנה ארגוני, כוח אדם, ריכוזיות ותלות במבחן יחיד שקובע את עתיד התלמידים.

tasks.prompt: What happened after the medical entrance paper was leaked in June?
options: The NTA abolished all engineering tests
More than two million students had to retake the exam, protests followed and the education minister resigned
Only 24 students were asked to sit another test
Universities immediately created unlimited places
tasks.correct_answer: More than two million students had to retake the exam, protests followed and the education minister resigned
tasks.explanation_hebrew: בעקבות הדליפה יותר משני מיליון תלמידים נבחנו מחדש, פרצו מחאות צעירים ושר החינוך הפדרלי התפטר.

tasks.prompt: Which staffing fact does BJ Rao identify as a weakness at the NTA?
options: All 221 employees are permanent academics
Only 24 of 221 employees are permanent, and many staff come from bureaucratic rather than assessment backgrounds
The agency employs no contract workers
Every employee specialises in computer security
tasks.correct_answer: Only 24 of 221 employees are permanent, and many staff come from bureaucratic rather than assessment backgrounds
tasks.explanation_hebrew: ראו מצביע על כך שרק 24 מתוך 221 העובדים קבועים, ושחסר כוח אדם בעל ניסיון אקדמי ומקצועי בהפעלת בחינות.

tasks.prompt: Why does the creation of another task force produce a sense of déjà vu?
options: Nandan Nilekani led every exam before 2017
A similar committee proposed many reforms after a 2024 crisis, yet another major failure occurred
Students had never heard of examination reform
The new task force has already abolished the NTA
tasks.correct_answer: A similar committee proposed many reforms after a 2024 crisis, yet another major failure occurred
tasks.explanation_hebrew: גם ב־2024 הוקמה ועדה שהציעה מעל מאה רפורמות, אך רק מעט יותר ממחציתן יושמו במלואן והמשבר חזר.

tasks.prompt: What does “ad hoc centres” mean in Rao's criticism?
options: Permanent centres built to one national standard
Temporary or improvised centres arranged for particular examinations
Universities offering several test dates each year
Centres managed only by permanent NTA specialists
tasks.correct_answer: Temporary or improvised centres arranged for particular examinations
tasks.explanation_hebrew: ad hoc מתאר מרכזים זמניים או מאולתרים שהוקמו לצורך מסוים, במקום מערך קבוע וסטנדרטי.

tasks.prompt: What does “upend” mean when the article describes the effect of a cancelled exam?
options: Disrupt completely or overturn carefully made plans
Reduce the cost of private tuition
Guarantee a university place
Publish examination results early
tasks.correct_answer: Disrupt completely or overturn carefully made plans
tasks.explanation_hebrew: upend פירושו לשבש מן היסוד; ביטול מבחן יכול להפוך חודשים או שנים של הכנה ותכנון.

tasks.prompt: Explain the reforms experts propose for how India's major entrance examinations are delivered and structured.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש לציין לפחות שש הצעות מדויקות ולחבר כל הצעה לחולשה שהיא אמורה לצמצם.
expected_points: Move more decisively toward computer-based examinations
Invest in stronger digital infrastructure
Replace ad hoc venues with standardised state-controlled online centres
Reduce unnecessary human involvement to limit opportunities for leaks
Restructure NEET-UG along the lines of the engineering entrance examination
Use two stages rather than one decisive sitting
Hold multiple sessions with different question sets
Allow students to take important entrance exams more than once a year
Build professional academic, technical and operational staffing
Make the NTA a statutory institution with clearer oversight and accountability

tasks.prompt: Why do experts argue that technology alone cannot solve the crisis of trust?
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש להסביר לפחות ארבע מגבלות שאינן טכנולוגיות ולהתייחס למבנה המערכת ולכוח האדם.
expected_points: The NTA relies heavily on temporary contract staff
Only a small minority of employees are permanent
Many staff lack specialised academic or assessment experience
Oversight and accountability need structural reform
A single high-stakes day creates extreme consequences even if delivery is digital
Millions compete for a limited number of university places
Previous reform proposals were only partly implemented
Exam design, centralisation and institutional capacity remain problems
Students need multiple chances and resilience against cancellation or disruption

tasks.prompt: Summarise why confidence in the NTA has declined and the main arguments for reforming rather than abolishing it.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש לכלול את רצף הכשלים, השפעתם על תלמידים, יתרונות גוף ארצי והצורך בשינוי מבני רחב.
expected_points: The NTA was created in 2017 to make examinations fair, transparent and standardised
Repeated paper leaks, cancellations and errors have damaged confidence
More than two million students retook the recent medical entrance exam
A 2024 committee's reforms were only partly implemented
Students lose time, money and carefully planned academic years
Some activists and politicians want the agency abolished
Supporters say one national body can provide common security, technology and candidate services
Multiple replacement agencies could duplicate costs and create uneven safeguards
Experts call for permanent specialist staff and statutory status
They also want less dependence on one-off exams and more testing opportunities
Scarcity of university places creates pressures the NTA cannot solve alone

tasks.prompt: Write a policy briefing prioritising three reforms that could rebuild trust in India's examination system.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש לכתוב באנגלית, לבחור שלוש עדיפויות שונות, לבסס אותן בעובדות ולציין מגבלה אחת לפחות לכל פתרון.
expected_points: Choose reforms from technology, staffing, exam design, accountability or testing frequency
Support computer-based exams with standardised secure infrastructure
Recommend permanent specialist academic, technical and operational staff
Recommend multiple sessions, stages or annual opportunities
Explain how each priority reduces leaks, disruption or excessive one-day risk
Cite the two-million-student retest or repeated cancellations
Address implementation gaps from the earlier 100-plus recommendations
Acknowledge that digital systems can also fail or require investment
Acknowledge that reforming the NTA will not create more university places
Prefer measurable implementation and accountability over another list of proposals
Avoid claiming that any single reform guarantees no future leak
